title: 5 days Upper Lower (2 Uppers 2 Lowers + 1 Arm day) program review
summary: NH reviews Tonii's upper/lower plus arm day program, which he rates as good and close to a gentleman split. He nitpicks rep ranges and sandbagging, squat plus deadlift on the same day, machine isolation leg work, duplicated curls, and the strength vs hypertrophy split between days, and suggests many superset and giant set reorganizations.
claims: An upper/lower template with an added arm day resembles his gentleman split, which he considers superior
Bench 4 sets of 4-6 is good strength work but implies sandbagging: if you get 6 on set one, still getting 4 on set four means the weight was not fully challenging
Sandbagging is not always bad if used strategically; it is also affected by weight increments
Incline DB press 4x10-12 after heavy bench is the right complement: high-quality volume made possible by strength in reserve
8-10 is a good rep range for pull-ups
3 sets is a bit low for overhead press, but fine after incline press pre-fatigue; 6-8 is higher-volume pressing
Barbell rows fit well on upper days because the lumbar spine and posterior chain are not pre-fatigued from squats or deadlifts, lowering injury risk, though they need extra warm-up
Rowing 4x6-8 sandbagged keeps reps high quality and injury risk low; progression comes from repeating sets across the week
Dips after bench, incline press and OHP are the most removable exercise; very vertical dips shift more work to the triceps
Incline DB skull crushers 3x8-10 are excellent; the long head needs work and small muscles should not always be trained at very high reps or they never progress in strength or size
Face pulls 10-12 are too low: do 15-20 or AMRAP, preferably with a band; they are rehab-like external rotation work and weighted versions alter the strength curve
Lateral raises 3x10-12 is an excellent rep range
Do not put two non-superset strength movements back to back; place a superset between them
Barbell rows can be superset with almost anything because no other upper lift impairs rowing
Face pulls followed by lateral raises improves rear delt connection in a giant set
Avoid squatting and deadlifting as strength work in the same session; the second lift suffers, entering with a fatigued lumbar and thoracic spine
Train both knee flexion and hip hinge frequently for full leg development, but make the second one a variation at higher reps or sandbagged intensity
Isolating the quads alone is impossible and pointless; training the whole lower body frequently is how naturals get big legs
Single-leg press, leg extensions and leg curls have zero specificity to compounds; a compound saves time and feeds the squat and deadlift
He is not a fan of unilateral leg movements but does not call them bad
Leg day suggestion: squat strength work, hip hinge 4x8-12 or 4x6-10, then giant set of single-leg press, leg curl and calf raises
Three sets of deadlifts at 4-6 is already a lot; deadlifts must be taken very seriously for fatigue management
Leg days should be minimalistic and shorter than upper days, but this one goes too far
Ab isolation is the way to bigger abs; after squats and deadlifts do them hanging for spinal decompression
Close-grip bench at 4 sets would benefit from 6-10 instead of 6-8 to widen the progression window
Chest flies 4x10-12 should be sandbagged to the max; the injury risk is high and you just want a good weighted stretch
If you stall on overhead press, lower rep ranges can save you through higher intensity
EZ bar curls and hammer curls back to back are a problem: small muscles recover slowly within a workout, so space them
Triceps isolation was concentrated on day 3; move V-bar pushdowns to day 1
Straight-bar pulldowns are the most expendable exercise; just do more pull-ups
Bench, OHP and pull-ups can be superset; squats and deadlifts he will never superset
Replace dumbbell shrugs by shrugging to failure at the top of a deadlift after rows; shrug strength exceeds rowing strength so you get lots of trap volume quickly
Trap hypertrophy comes from weighted stretch, such as heavy rack pulls or snatch-grip shrugs, which beat dumbbell shrugs
Skewing days toward strength or hypertrophy is good, but day 2 went too far toward strength and day 3 too far toward hypertrophy
Going from 4x4-6 to 4x6-8 on squats is a big tonnage jump; better to repeat 4-6 and add a knee-flexion variation like paused squats
Leg press and leg extensions duplicate each other; drop one and do more knee flexion work
Sandbagging works on upper days where sets echo each other, but not on minimalist leg days where nothing afterwards feeds the squat
An arm day needs compound movements, or you are wasting your time; every day needs a strength component
Close-grip bench repeats well because it is easy on the shoulders, but it and behind-the-head long head work can be hard on the elbows
Arm days are the most personal day of a program
Add forearm isolation, shoulder isolation and face pulls to arm day giant sets; arms are small enough to superset
exercises: fits upper day, low injury risk
Single-leg press / leg extension / leg curl
shrug to failure after the last rep
